n.quote: Replication results: In the replication experiment, the average number of potential dates for people who inadvertently did not answer all questions on their desirable behaviors was 7.134 (sd = 1.860; n = 605), while the average number of potential dates for people who deliberately did not provide answers to all questions was 7.057 (sd = 2.066; n = 619). The difference of 0.077 (se = 0.112) was tested using an independent samples t-test (t(1222) = 0.688, p = 0.492; n = 1224). As a result, we cannot reject the null hypothesis of no difference in the number of dates of inadvertent nondisclosers and hiders. The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = 0.039 (95% CI [–0.073, 0.151]).
